title: shutup-and-run worker config (config.json)
description: The one config file of a worker: /etc/shutup-and-run/config.json (on Windows, inside the shutup-and-run WSL distribution). `shutup-and-run config` and the local page read and write it; nothing else holds config. The service applies more rules than a schema can say (for example default_timeout_secs <= max_timeout_secs); `shutup-and-run config validate` is the authority. Unknown keys are rejected.

poll_url.description: Where the worker asks for work, every poll_interval_secs. http or https, no credentials in it. It may carry a filter in the query, for example ?user=ana; that filter is not a secret. Unset: the worker polls nothing and is idle.

worker_name.description: Sent in the poll body so one URL can serve many machines. Printable ASCII, no spaces or quotes. Default: the host name.

allowlist.description: Image repositories this machine may run. `repo` allows repo:tag and repo@digest. May be empty only with poll_any_image.

poll_any_image.description: A task from poll_url may name any image. A pushed job never skips the allowlist. Needs poll_url.

default_timeout_secs.description: Time limit of a job that names none.

max_timeout_secs.description: Longest time limit a job may ask for. At most 7 days.

token.description: Bearer token of this machine's HTTP API. Secret: masked in `config show`, in the page and in reports.

poll_token.description: Bearer token sent to poll_url: who this machine is to the queue. Secret. Changing it makes the machine a new one that the poll URL has to approve.

admin_user.description: Login of the advanced settings on the local page.

admin_password.description: Password of that login. Not strong: it keeps a curious person out. Secret.

listen.description: Address and port of the API and the local page.

http.description: Plain HTTP. For localhost or a private network. false needs tls_cert and tls_key.

status_page.description: The local page at GET /, for a loopback peer only. Also: a pause does not outlive a restart.

worker_os.description: Sent in the poll body. `windows` inside the WSL distribution. Default: the OS of the binary.

resource_profile.description: shared-pc: the machine is someone's everyday computer. Each job gets at most 1 CPU and 2g of memory with no extra swap, and no new job starts with less than 2g of memory or 5g of disk free; on a machine (on Windows, the WSL2 VM) with under 4g the two memory figures are half of what it has. none: no such defaults. Default: shared-pc when worker_os is windows, otherwise none. The four keys below replace one figure each, under either profile.

max_job_cpus.description: The most CPU one job may ask for, and what a job that asks for none gets, as `docker run --cpus` counts: "1", "0.5". From 0.01 to 128. A job that asks for more is refused. A string, so it reads the same in the CLI and the file.

max_job_memory.description: The same for memory: "2g", "512m". At least 6m. The container gets no swap beyond it.

min_free_memory.description: No new job starts while less memory than this is available (MemAvailable where the service runs; on Windows that is the WSL2 VM, not the PC). "0" turns the check off.

min_free_disk.description: No new job starts while the disk Docker writes to has less than this free. "0" turns the check off.

history_path.description: SQLite job history. status.json is written beside it.

history_days.description: Days a finished job stays in the history.

docker_config.description: Directory of a Docker config.json with registry credentials.

log_lines.description: Lines of a container's log kept with its job.

reaper_interval_secs.description: How often time limits are checked.

purge_interval_secs.description: How often old history is deleted.

prune_interval_secs.description: How often unused images are pruned. 0: never.

auth_failures.description: Wrong tokens from one address before it is banned.

trust_x_forwarded_for.description: Take the caller's address from X-Forwarded-For. Only behind your own proxy.
